business_summary.text: Inventurus Knowledge Solutions (IKS Health) provides technology-enabled care enablement and revenue cycle management services to US healthcare provider organisations, and after the TruBridge acquisition also sells EHR systems to the rural and community hospital market.

call_points.text: Management aims to scale EBITDA from ~₹1,000 Cr to ₹3,000 Cr by FY30 while reducing net debt close to zero.
Headcount grew 5.3% YoY to 13,331 as of March 31, 2026, highlighting non-linear revenue expansion over workforce growth.
Gross debt was reduced to ₹251 Cr as of March 31, 2026 from its peak of ₹850 Cr, funded by strong cash flows.
Effective tax rate is expected to be around 22% for FY27 for the standalone IKS business.
Modernization of TruBridge's EHR from COBOL to PostgreS will be an 18 to 24 month process.
Customer base has been pared down from 700+ to around 600 provider organizations, cutting the tail of small legacy AQuity clients.

operating_notes.text: Combined entity will support >2,000 healthcare organizations and >150,000 clinicians.
Q4FY26 revenue grew 18% YoY in INR and 13% YoY in USD terms.
Company approved acquiring 100% of Arai Solutions Private Limited for ₹11 Cr to enhance AI R&D capabilities.
IKS Health announced the acquisition of ARAI Solutions to integrate biomedical knowledge graphs and build a full agentic AI stack.
Headcount reached 13,331 as of March 31, 2026 (+5.3% YoY), including 1,981 clinical staff and 550 tech FTEs.
Top 10 clients grew 28% YoY in FY26, representing an average relationship vintage of over 5 years.
Legacy IKS run-rate is about $97 million a quarter ($388 million annualised) and TruBridge about $75 million a quarter ($300 million annualised), for a combined $688 million revenue business.
Top 10 customer vintage is about six years and top five about seven years, with top-10 and top-5 revenue contribution flat versus Q4.
Adjusted FCF yield was 90% in the quarter after adjusting for a one-time NEVA customer payment; return on equity was 26%.

timeline.summary: Inventurus Knowledge Solutions agreed to acquire US-based TruBridge Inc. for up to USD 565 million, funded via USD 670 million in debt facilities.
IKS Health to acquire US-based TruBridge for up to $565 mn via debt, adding 1,500+ clients
IKS Health signs definitive agreement to acquire US-based TruBridge at $26.25 per share
Inventurus Knowledge Solutions agreed to acquire US-based TruBridge Inc. for an enterprise value of $557 million.
IKS Health signed a strategic multi-year care enablement and revenue optimization partnership with 219-bed Holyoke Medical Center.
Rekha Timblo, Ashwini Gupta, and Ashra Family Trust confirmed no encumbrances on Inventurus Knowledge Solutions’ shares held by promoter group members during FY 2025-26.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹857.65 Cr (+18.5% YoY), net profit ₹205.97 Cr (+39.4% YoY).
Inventurus Knowledge Solutions reported FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹3,194 Cr up 20% YoY and PAT of ₹722 Cr up 48% YoY.
Inventurus Knowledge Solutions approved the acquisition of Arai Solutions Private Limited for ₹11 Cr in cash.
IKS Health announced the acquisition of artificial intelligence management and technology company ARAI Solutions on May 13, 2026.
Sameer Chavan, Company Secretary, shared Q4 FY 2025-26 earnings conference call recording on May 14, 2026, available at ikshealth.com/ir/2026/q4/q4-earnings-call-recording.mp3.
IKS Health hosted its Q4FY26 earnings call, reiterating its FY30 EBITDA target of ₹3,000 Cr and detailing the $1.2M ARAI acquisition.
Shareholders approved postal ballot resolutions for pledge/disposal of material subsidiary shares/assets and financial guarantees for US subsidiary Inventurus Knowledge Solutions, Inc.

watchlist.response: Outcome-based pricing (% of customer revenue) insulates margins; pricing deflation is seen in simple point solutions but mitigated by full platform bundling.
watchlist.text: Clients demanding pricing deflation or productivity gains back as AI adoption grows

watchlist.response: Quarterly variations occur due to RCM seasonality; investors should evaluate customer concentration on an annual basis where top clients show robust growth.
watchlist.text: Quarterly variance in top 10 customer revenue concentration

watchlist.response: Sachin Gupta said 12% growth came on 4.2% headcount growth and is driven by operating efficiencies, not currency; aspiration is north of 12% constant currency but explicitly not guidance.
watchlist.text: Satyam Kumar asked what constant-currency growth is sustainable organically, noting 12% this quarter was among the slowest since listing and asking whether margin gains came from currency.

watchlist.response: Management said it cannot give a TruBridge revenue growth outlook yet and needs two to three quarters; only the legacy IKS 12%-plus aspiration was repeated.
watchlist.text: Aditi asked for a consolidated pro-forma revenue outlook after TruBridge consolidation and revenue synergies.

watchlist.response: Sachin Gupta said yes, because EBITDA is unchanged despite lower revenue, and it may be slightly more EPS accretive than imagined.
watchlist.text: Mayank Babla asked whether FY27 remains EPS accretive given the TruBridge revenue rationalisation not foreseen before the acquisition.

watchlist.response: Management cited technology deployment and offshore human-in-the-loop to reach early-to-mid 30s blended margin, and said the ₹3,000 Cr target does not require acquisitions but doors remain open.
watchlist.text: Madhuchanda Dey asked what the low-hanging levers are to lift TruBridge's 22-23% EBITDA margin and whether the no-dilution FY30 target rules out large acquisitions.
